question: How much is the excess on my Essential policy if my son's driving, he's twenty-two?
expected_answer: On DriveGuard Essential the standard excess is AED 500 per claim, and drivers under 25 pay an additional AED 1,000, so AED 1,500 in total.

key_facts: Standard excess: AED 500 per claim
Drivers under 25 years old
an additional excess of AED 1,000 on top of the standard excess

question: So if the repair's three thousand and the excess is four hundred, how much do you cover?
expected_answer: You pay the first 400 yourself and the insurer pays the remaining 2,600 of the approved repair cost.

history.text: I scraped my car on a pillar in a mall car park.
No, it's just the bumper, but the claim form keeps mentioning an excess.
No problem, I can go through that with you.

key_facts: the insurer pays 2,600
you pay the 400 excess yourself

question: I'm on Essential and my car's eight months old, do you deduct depreciation on parts?
expected_answer: Yes. DriveGuard Essential deducts a flat 15% from the cost of every replaced part on every claim, from the first day of cover and regardless of the car's age; only windscreen and window glass is replaced in full.

key_facts: a flat 15% is deducted from the cost of every replaced part on every claim
regardless of the vehicle's age
meta.common_prior: No, a car under one or two years old normally has no depreciation deducted on replaced parts.

question: What does agency repair on Premier actually mean for me, my car's four years old?
expected_answer: On DriveGuard Premier, cars up to 5 years old from first registration are repaired at the manufacturer's authorised agency workshop, so your four-year-old car goes to the agency; older cars go to an approved non-agency garage.

key_facts: cars up to 5 years old from first registration are repaired at the manufacturer's authorised agency workshop

question: What does depreciation on parts mean when you guys fix my car?
expected_answer: It means the insurer deducts a percentage from the cost of new replacement parts to allow for the wear on the old parts they replace, and you pay that share yourself.

key_facts: a percentage is deducted from the cost of new replacement parts
you pay the deducted share

question: How long have I usually got to report a small accident to you?
expected_answer: You must notify within 24 hours of the accident, with the police report; late notification without a good reason can lead to the claim being declined.

key_facts: notify Liwan Crest Insurance within 24 hours of the accident
late notification without a good reason, such as being in hospital, can lead to the claim being declined
meta.common_prior: As soon as reasonably possible, typically within 7 to 30 days.

question: How soon after I report it will your surveyor come and look at the car?
expected_answer: Within 2 working days of notification, at the Al Quoz survey centre or free of charge at your home or workplace in Dubai, Sharjah or Abu Dhabi.

key_facts: Our surveyor inspects the car within 2 working days of notification
free of charge, at your home or workplace

question: Why does someone normally need to inspect my car before it's repaired?
expected_answer: The inspection lets the insurer confirm the damage matches the accident, check what's covered, and agree the repair method and cost with the garage before work starts.

key_facts: to confirm the damage and what is covered
to agree the repair method and cost before work starts

question: Uh, if I just get my windscreen replaced, does that touch my no-claims discount?
expected_answer: Yes. A windscreen or window glass replacement is treated as an at-fault claim and reduces your NCD by two steps at renewal; only a chip repair has no effect.

key_facts: we treat a windscreen or window glass replacement as an at-fault claim
reduces your NCD by two steps
Only a chip repair
meta.common_prior: No, windscreen claims usually don't affect the no-claims discount.

question: Um, does the no-claims discount stay with me or with the car if I sell it?
expected_answer: The no-claims discount belongs to you as the policyholder, not the vehicle, because it reflects your own claim-free driving, so it can move with you to your next car's policy.

key_facts: the no-claims discount belongs to the policyholder, not the car
it can be transferred to a new car

question: Does roadside cover me if I get stuck in sand just off the road?
expected_answer: No. Roadside assistance covers paved and public roads only, with no off-road or desert recovery even if the car is a few metres off the road, so you'd need a private recovery service at your own cost.

key_facts: covers paved and public roads only
We do not provide off-road or desert recovery
even if the car is only a few metres off the road
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, roadside assistance will send recovery to wherever your car is stuck.

question: How far will you tow it for free? My garage is out in Deira.
expected_answer: On DriveGuard Premier towing is covered up to 100 km per call-out; anything beyond that is charged at AED 5 per km.

history.text: Hi, my car's broken down on the Hatta road.
Sorry to hear that. Are you somewhere safe?
Yes, I'm on the hard shoulder. I'm on the Premier plan.
Okay, I'll arrange a tow truck for you now.

key_facts: towing up to 100 km per call-out
AED 5 per km

question: Why would I need roadside assistance if I've already got comprehensive cover?
expected_answer: Comprehensive cover pays for damage from accidents, theft and so on, while roadside assistance is a service that gets help to you when the car breaks down, like a flat battery, a puncture or a tow to a garage.

key_facts: comprehensive pays for damage to the car
roadside assistance helps with breakdowns such as a flat battery or a tow

question: Why did you write my car off instead of just, um, fixing it?
expected_answer: A car is treated as a total loss when the estimated repair cost is more than 60% of its insured value; you're then paid the insured value less the excess.

key_facts: the estimated repair cost is more than 60% of the insured value
pay the insured value less the excess

question: The report says it could be a total loss, what does that mean for me?
expected_answer: A total loss means the car is too badly damaged to be worth repairing, or can't be repaired safely, so instead of fixing it the insurer pays out its covered value and usually takes the wreck.

history.text: Your surveyor looked at my car after the flood on Monday.
Yes, I can see his report on your file now.

key_facts: the car is not worth repairing
the insurer pays out the car's value instead of repairing it

question: Can I cancel my car insurance halfway through and get the rest back?
expected_answer: Only if the car is sold or transferred, exported or deregistered. With no claims, the refund then follows a short-period scale, not pro rata (for example 45% if cancelled within 6 months), less an AED 100 administration fee.
answer_aliases: only if the car is sold

key_facts: cannot be cancelled mid-term while the car is still registered in your name
short-period scale, not pro rata
administration fee of AED 100
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, you can cancel any time and get a pro-rata refund for the unused months, minus a small admin fee.

question: What happens if I've only got third-party cover and I hit a wall?
expected_answer: Third-party cover only pays for injury or damage you cause to other people and their property, so it would pay for the wall's owner but not for the damage to your own car.

key_facts: third-party cover pays for damage to other people's property
damage to your own car is not covered

question: What happens if I renew my car insurance a few days late?
expected_answer: Motor policies have no grace period: cover ends at 11:59 pm on the expiry date, so you're uninsured until you renew and can't legally drive.

key_facts: there is no grace period for motor policies
Cover ends at 11:59 pm on the expiry date
meta.common_prior: You're usually still covered during a grace period of around 15 to 30 days.

question: How early can I renew the car policy without, um, losing days of cover?
expected_answer: You can renew up to 30 days before expiry without losing any days of cover, because the new policy starts the day after the old one ends.

key_facts: renew up to 30 days in advance without losing any days of cover

question: My son's just turned twenty, why do you charge him so much for cover?
expected_answer: Young and newly licensed drivers are statistically much more likely to have accidents and claim, so insurers price that higher risk into their premiums.

key_facts: young drivers have a higher accident and claim risk
higher risk means a higher premium

question: What's the most you'll pay for one item, like my new laptop, under contents?
expected_answer: Any one item is covered up to AED 7,500 unless it's listed separately on your schedule.
answer_aliases: seven and a half thousand dirhams

key_facts: any one item is covered up to AED 7,500 unless it is listed separately on the schedule

question: If a pipe bursts and floods my flat, is all of that covered?
expected_answer: Your belongings are covered for sudden escape of water from a burst pipe, but not the building itself, not gradual leakage, and a water damage claim carries a higher AED 1,000 excess.

key_facts: sudden escape of water from burst pipes
It does not cover the building itself
excess of AED 1,000
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, burst pipe water damage is fully covered under home insurance.

question: I've heard I might be underinsured on contents, why would that hurt my claim?
expected_answer: You're underinsured when your sum insured is lower than the full cost of replacing everything you own; the insurer can then cut claims in proportion, so you get less than your actual loss.

key_facts: sum insured is less than the full replacement value
claims can be reduced in proportion

question: I booked my flights like a month ago, can I still get cancellation cover now?
expected_answer: Not for that trip: cancellation cover applies only if the policy was bought within 7 days of paying the first deposit or booking payment. Buying now still gives you medical, baggage and delay cover.

key_facts: within 7 days of the date you paid the first deposit or booking payment
still covers medical, baggage and delay, but not cancellation
meta.common_prior: Yes, you can buy cancellation cover any time before departure, as long as the reason for cancelling hasn't arisen yet.

question: So what's the difference in cancellation cover between single trip and annual?
expected_answer: Voyager Single Trip pays trip cancellation up to AED 7,500, while Voyager Annual Multi-Trip pays up to AED 10,000 per trip, each per insured person.

key_facts: trip cancellation up to AED 7,500
trip cancellation up to AED 10,000 per trip

question: What's the difference between trip cancellation and curtailment on a travel policy?
expected_answer: Cancellation covers costs you lose if you have to call off the trip before you leave; curtailment covers unused costs and extra expenses if you have to cut the trip short and come home early.

key_facts: cancellation applies before you depart
curtailment applies when you cut the trip short

question: Okay, and is there a limit on how long each trip can be?
expected_answer: Each trip can last up to 45 days; a longer trip isn't covered at all for any day of it unless you extend with us before it reaches 45 days.

history.text: We travel a lot for work, so I'm looking at the annual multi-trip plan.
Sure, that one covers as many trips as you like during the year.

key_facts: Each trip can last up to 45 days
not covered at all for any day of that trip

question: How long does an annual multi-trip policy last, from when exactly?
expected_answer: An annual multi-trip policy runs for twelve months from the start date shown on the policy, covering trips that begin within that year.

key_facts: twelve months from the policy start date

question: Do I need to book for the survey centre on a Saturday, or can I walk in?
expected_answer: The Al Quoz survey centre is open Monday to Saturday, 7:30 am to 6:00 pm, for inspections by appointment, but walk-ins are accepted before 3:00 pm.

key_facts: open Monday to Saturday, 7:30 am to 6:00 pm
Walk-ins are accepted before 3:00 pm

question: What should I do first after a small accident, like, before I call you?
expected_answer: First make sure everyone is safe and call emergency services if anyone is hurt; then take photos of the scene and the damage, exchange details with the other driver, and report it to the police where the law requires it.

key_facts: make sure everyone is safe first
take photos and exchange details with the other driver
